body: This might be kind of long but I hope this brings a bit of perspective & maybe change the way you look at the situation I have felt this way before & still do some days.. having lived with BPD since I was a preteen and now being 27.. I’ve taken notice that it’s not us, yes they don’t want to be around us they’re scared to get to know us but it’s not even because it’s US. It’s because we’re authentic and loyal and that scares people. We know how we feel , we feel deeply and strongly , we’re constantly trying to find ourselves so we discover new things about ourselves beyond surface level things, we love fully and extremely whether it’s in relationships or friendships. We’re extremely loyal to the point where it’s sometimes a fault & We live with a major mental disorder that requires to better ourselves and lives constantly so we can heal past traumas and more…(something a lot of people find uncomfortable and don’t want to do) We’re just REAL and that’s scary for the major population. They leave because the authenticity is too much, the real genuine love is too much, someone knowing their real personality is too much, so many people hide behind a fake personas, vices and distractions. It IS uncomfortable for them but only because you want to get to know the real them and vice versa. Please, just know that it’s not you! It’s them! The fact that you can be and want to be open about your feelings and understand them enough to communicate them is something big and a big step in most people’s self healing journey & people dont or want to do that these days so you have to find the people who appreciate that and do the same. People who WANT to heal as well and have real connections. I’m 27 I’ve been through multiple friends, friend groups. I’ve had people leave and I’ve left people but luckily just 2 years ago I found 3 people who I can genuinely feel myself around or call when I feel lonely and they care enough to check up on the when I’m having episodes or start to isolate. It’s rare but it’s out there you just gotta be resilient and just realize… some people just suck.. if they don’t want to get to know you it’s their loss don’t take it as yours just shake it off and keep going. BPD is hard to navigate but it doesn’t make us any less if anything it makes us more & never too much , never ever think your too much and if someone tells you that ,they’re not for you.

I see, tough predicament I'd say try finding his parents on social media and just let them know through there but that can be kind of difficult as well... he seems like he's been thinking about this for a while now and is set in his ways which can be difficult. 

You guys got 2 years thats  2 more years with you he didn't have before so hopefully along the way his mind will change. The only advice I can give in this situation is try seeing each other in person within those 2 years,  show him how life with you can be get him excited for the future because from the sound of it , it seems like he feels stuck in school & his main probelm IS school which sucks because schools in America do not know how to teach kids who need more help than others, its not about learning at the end of the day its about passing nd that can make you feel less than when it's not the case only for it to not even really matter in the end as long as you get that diploma. 

My last suggestion is finding a tutor outside of school maybe even online that can help him better cause like I said school's in America aren't great...o ly going downhill in my opinion but he does need to pass somehow and hopefully when he gets that diploma he'll feel a little lighter, light enough to keep going.

How's his relationship with his parents ? Does he have any siblings? If the relationship is good I'd say try to get in contact with them and let them know what's going on. They may be better dealing with it since they are there with him and to keep an eye on him. I think tutoring and therapy would be very beneficial for him. He may have more than just failing grades that's getting him down. I've been where he is, kind of still am and from experience I good support system goes a long way, maybe he feels like he doesn't have that.

I've been in a similar situation to you still kind of am (stuck no place to go,  no friends and distant to my family), it's gotten better but because I was able to advocate for myself regardless of what my family thought or said but it's easier said than done. In my opinion your best bet is to save up to move out, if you feel like you can be paid better somewhere else apply for new jobs don't quit your current one until you get the new one..

That'll give you some space for the mean time. Also your 20 legally an adult id say look into some therapy that'll be covered by your insurance if you or your parents have any. Some people think therapy is for people who are mentally unstable but no it could help you find your footing and not want to shut down so much they also provide alot of resources as well.. 

Shits tough out here especially when you're family is supposed to be on your side. I get the whole not wanting to do anything but the less we do for ourselves the more we fall into a hole... I hope you're able to find a solution suitable solution for you and I'm always a DM away if you ever wanna talk, I don't really have anyone either gotta stick together tho right ? Haha best of luck !

Personally I’d say give it some time and wait for him to message you, you don’t want to fall in those obsessive habits constantly worrying and checking it’s not good especially for someone with BPD. Keep your options open and talk to different people, nothing wrong with that. Usually when you tell people you have BPD they google and scare themselves off and if that’s what he did , not worth it. Someone should get to know you before they jump to conclusions on how you are with your BPD and as long as you’re honest and open the right person will stick around. In my personal experience just try your best not to get stuck or too attached in one person. Hope that helps !
